metadata.summary: Attach one file to a ticket, project task, client, contact or asset
metadata.description: Attaches ONE file to a ticket, project_task, client, contact or asset. Prefer source.type=url: give an https URL and the server downloads it (max size is the tenant storage limit). The URL host must be on the workspace's allowed download hosts (a tenant admin manages the list under Settings > MCP Server > Allowed download hosts; the ChatGPT file host is built in). If the call fails with 400 FETCH_HOST_NOT_ALLOWED, nothing was downloaded: tell the user an admin can add that host, and do not retry with other URLs. Use source.type=base64 only for small content you wrote yourself, never to relay a user's file, and file_name is then required. One file per call; make several calls for several files. In an MCP client with the attach_file tool, use that instead. Returns 201 with the stored document; 400 for a disallowed type, oversize file, unfetchable URL or a host that is not allowed (FETCH_HOST_NOT_ALLOWED), 403 without permission, 404 for a missing record.

metadata.description: Downloads the original stored file for a document as an attachment. The documentId path value is resolved against documents.document_id first, then documents.file_id. The route supports Auth.js session-cookie authentication and x-api-key fallback for machine clients, derives the tenant from the authenticated principal, requires document:read permission, and runs document authorization rules before reading the file from storage. To read what is inside an attachment (image, PDF, document), use the read_attachment tool instead: this endpoint returns raw file bytes, which call_api_endpoint cannot show you.

Downloads a stored document file, or exports the document as PDF or Markdown based on the optional format query parameter. The fileId path value may be either a documents.document_id or an external_files.file_id. The route supports Auth.js session-cookie authentication and x-api-key fallback for machine clients (internal users only; client-portal keys are refused), and runs within the authenticated principal's tenant. Every format uses document read permission and document authorization rules. To read what is inside an attachment (image, PDF, document), use the read_attachment tool instead: this endpoint returns raw file bytes, which call_api_endpoint cannot show you.
